2609.08248.title: Agentic ML Exploration (A-MLE) for Ads Ranking
2609.08248.paper_summary: Modern industrial ads ranking stacks are increasingly bottlenecked not by model capacity or training compute, but by the throughput of human ML iteration - the cycles of research, implementation, training, debugging, evaluation, and launch required to surface a single statistically significant improvement. A typical ranking stack contains numerous differentiated models with heterogeneous data, architectures, and infrastructure constraints, and each cycle takes days to weeks of senior engineer attention per model. As a result, techniques that have proven effective on one model diffuse into others slowly and unevenly, leaving substantial recoverable signal unexplored. We present Agentic ML Exploration (A-MLE), an autonomous LLM-agent system that systematically explores ML techniques across a portfolio of ads ranking models. A-MLE decomposes ML iteration into five stages involving hypothesis generation, exploration strategy, experiment execution, result analysis and shared knowledge substrate which are orchestrated by a single agent that invokes domain-specific skills and agentic workflows against a sandboxed execution layer, with human-in-the-loop checkpoints at each stage boundary. We deploy A-MLE across a representative set of large-scale ads ranking models and evaluate it along a tiered capability framework (tool availability, autonomous workflow execution, and open-ended exploration). We further report a controlled cross-LLM study using a fixed agent loop, which surfaces qualitative differences in execution reliability and exploration aggressiveness across the Claude Sonnet, Gemini, and GPT families. We discuss failure modes and the design choices that govern reliability. Our findings suggest that agentic exploration is a practical force multiplier for ML engineers in industrial recommenders, especially for the long tail of models that rarely receive expert attention.
2609.08248.paper_summary_zh: 現代工業廣告排名系統的瓶頸越來越不是模型容量或訓練計算能力，而是人類機器學習迭代的通量——為了發掘單一統計上顯著的改進所需的研究、實施、訓練、調試、評估和發布的循環。典型的排名系統包含多個具有異質數據、架構和基礎設施限制的差異化模型，每個模型的每個循環都需要數天到數週的資深工程師的注意。因此，已在一個模型上證明有效的技術在其他模型中的擴散速度緩慢且不均勻，留下了大量可回收的信號未被探索。我們提出了Agentic ML Exploration (A-MLE)，這是一個自主的LLM代理系統，系統地探索一組廣告排名模型中的機器學習技術。A-MLE將機器學習迭代分解為五個階段，包括假設生成、探索策略、實驗執行、結果分析和共享知識基底，這些階段由一個單一代理協調，該代理在沙盒執行層上調用領域特定的技能和代理工作流程，每個階段邊界都有人工介入的檢查點。我們在一組具有代表性的超大型廣告排名模型上部署A-MLE，並根據分層能力框架（工具可用性、自主工作流程執行和開放式探索）對其進行評估。我們還報告了一項使用固定代理循環的受控跨LLM研究，該研究揭示了Claude Sonnet、Gemini和GPT系列在執行可靠性和探索積極性方面的定性差異。我們討論了失敗模式和影響可靠性的設計選擇。我們的研究結果表明，代理探索對工業推薦系統中的機器學習工程師來說是一種實用的力量倍增器，特別是對於那些很少受到專家關注的長尾模型。
